title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity
seo_title: Classification of Elements and Periodicity Class 11 Chemistry Worksheet (NCERT Ch 3)
standard_code: Class 11 Chemistry, Chapter 3: Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties
standard_text: Significance of classification, brief history of the development of the periodic table, modern periodic law and the present form of the periodic table, periodic trends in properties of elements – atomic radii, ionic radii, inert gas radii, ionisation enthalpy, electron gain enthalpy, electronegativity, valency. Nomenclature of elements with atomic number greater than 100.
meta_desc: Free CBSE Class 11 Chemistry worksheets for NCERT Chapter 3 Classification of Elements and Periodicity in Properties: periods, groups and blocks, IUPAC names above 100, atomic radius, ionisation enthalpy and electronegativity. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: The modern periodic law is based on atomic number.
key_sub: Across a period radius falls and ionisation enthalpy rises; down a group the opposite.
body_html:
How to think about it

The modern periodic table arranges elements by atomic number into 7 periods and 18 groups. The block (s, p, d, f) is set by the orbital that the last electron enters. The period is the highest shell number. Elements above Z = 100 have temporary IUPAC names built from digit roots: nil, un, bi, tri, quad, pent, hex, sept, oct, enn + ium.

Across a period nuclear charge increases, so atomic radius falls and ionisation enthalpy and electronegativity rise. Down a group new shells are added, so radius rises. Exceptions such as N > O and Be > B in ionisation enthalpy come from stable half-filled and filled subshells.

Example

Z = 20 (Ca). Period and group?

[Ar] 4s²

Answer: period 4, group 2

Example

Z = 114. IUPAC name?

un-un-quad-ium

Answer: ununquadium

Common mistakes

  • Using atomic mass instead of atomic number.
  • Writing the IUPAC name as 'biium'.
  • Thinking a cation is larger than its atom.

faq.q: Why does atomic radius decrease across a period?
faq.a: The nuclear charge increases while electrons enter the same shell, so they are pulled closer.

faq.q: Why is the first ionisation enthalpy of N greater than that of O?
faq.a: N has a stable half-filled 2p³ subshell; in O one 2p electron is paired and easier to remove.
